questions.question: An EMT manages difficult calls well but has stopped sleeping adequately and seeing friends. Which plan best supports resilience over time?

choices.text: Protect recovery time, maintain supportive relationships, and use healthy routines
Build resilience mainly by taking more difficult calls
Keep the schedule and use caffeine to replace lost sleep
Reserve self-care changes until job performance declines

questions.explanation: Resilience involves coping and recovering; rest, relationships, and healthy habits support that recovery.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: More exposure without recovery can increase cumulative stress.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: A stimulant does not replace adequate sleep or social support.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Preventive habits should precede noticeable performance failure.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Resilience involves coping and recovering; rest, relationships, and healthy habits support that recovery.

questions.question: What is an infectious disease?

choices.text: A disease caused by harmful organisms within the body
A disease that necessarily spreads directly from one person to another
A disease that results from a physical injury
A disease defined by a harmful immune response to an otherwise harmless substance

questions.explanation: An infectious disease is caused by harmful organisms within the body. A communicable disease can spread between people or species.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Spread is the additional feature of communicability; it is not required to define every infectious disease.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Physical injury is not the definition of an infectious disease.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: This describes an allergic response rather than an infection.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Infectious describes the cause; communicable describes the ability to spread.

questions.question: Late in a shift, an EMT repeatedly loses focus and nearly falls asleep before driving. What is the best response?

choices.text: Report the impairment and arrange a safe fatigue-management response
Drink caffeine and begin driving while waiting for it to work
Drive with the window open and rely on the partner to keep talking
Complete the next transport before reporting the fatigue

questions.explanation: Impaired alertness threatens driving and patient-care safety; address the risk before a preventable incident.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Caffeine may improve alertness temporarily but does not establish fitness to drive immediately.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Conversation or airflow does not resolve dangerous impairment.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Deferring the report leaves the known hazard in place.

sourceReferences.locator: II.C: Sleep deprivation and fatigue management

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Impaired alertness threatens driving and patient-care safety; address the risk before a preventable incident.
questions.whyNotBest: Caffeine may improve alertness temporarily but does not establish fitness to drive immediately.
questions.keyDistinction: Impaired alertness threatens driving and patient-care safety; address the risk before a preventable incident.

questions.question: A coughing patient is suspected of having infectious pulmonary tuberculosis. The patient can tolerate a mask and does not need oxygen. Which pairing best provides source control and provider respiratory protection?

choices.text: Surgical mask on the patient; fit-tested N95 or higher-level respirator on the provider
N95 on the patient; surgical mask on the provider
Surgical masks on both patient and provider
N95 on the provider; omit patient masking because the provider is protected

questions.explanation: Patient masking limits release of infectious particles; a suitable respirator protects the provider from airborne exposure.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: This reverses the source-control and provider-protection roles.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: A surgical mask is not a substitute for the provider’s airborne respirator.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Provider protection does not replace source control when the patient can tolerate it.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Patient masking limits release of infectious particles; a suitable respirator protects the provider from airborne exposure.
questions.whyTempting: Both masks may seem interchangeable when both people are masked.
questions.whyNotBest: This reverses the source-control and provider-protection roles.
questions.keyDistinction: Patient masking limits release of infectious particles; a suitable respirator protects the provider from airborne exposure.

questions.question: An EMT expects substantial blood splatter while treating trauma. The patient has no known infectious diagnosis. Which PPE decision best applies standard precautions?

choices.text: Use gloves and appropriate eye, face, and clothing protection for the anticipated exposure
Use gloves alone until an infectious diagnosis is confirmed
Use gloves and a surgical mask, relying on prescription glasses for eye protection
Choose PPE only after asking whether the patient has hepatitis or HIV

questions.explanation: Standard precautions apply regardless of known diagnosis; the anticipated exposure determines needed protection.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Unknown infection status does not remove splash risk.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Ordinary prescription glasses do not provide adequate splash protection.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Patient history does not replace exposure-based precautions.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Standard precautions apply regardless of known diagnosis; the anticipated exposure determines needed protection.
questions.whyTempting: Gloves are a familiar first line of protection.
questions.whyNotBest: Unknown infection status does not remove splash risk.
questions.keyDistinction: Standard precautions apply regardless of known diagnosis; the anticipated exposure determines needed protection.

questions.question: Why does wearing an N95 respirator require a respiratory-protection program that includes fit testing?

choices.text: Filtering material alone is insufficient if air leaks around an unsuitable face seal
Fit testing replaces the need for the correct respirator type
The N95 rating means every wearer has an adequate seal
A surgical mask underneath necessarily corrects a poor fit

questions.explanation: A respirator must both filter particles and fit the wearer appropriately.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Correct selection remains necessary in addition to fit.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: The filtration rating does not establish individual fit.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: An extra mask does not establish an effective respirator seal.

sourceReferences.locator: III.F.9.e: Fit testing and OSHA guidelines

questions.question: After removing gloves, an EMT notices visible blood on their hands. A sink is available. Which sequence best addresses the contamination?

choices.text: Use soap and water, rub all hand surfaces including between fingers and around nails, then rinse and dry
Apply sanitizer briefly and put on clean gloves while the hands remain wet
Rinse with water only and dry because the blood came from the outside of the gloves
Scrub the palms with soap but avoid the fingertips to prevent irritating them

questions.explanation: Visible soil calls for soap and water; all hand surfaces need cleaning even after glove use.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Sanitizer alone is not the appropriate replacement for washing visibly soiled hands.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Water alone omits soap and friction, and glove removal does not negate contamination.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Fingertips, nails, and spaces between fingers are important areas to clean.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Visible soil calls for soap and water; all hand surfaces need cleaning even after glove use.

questions.question: Which pair describes two ways a person can acquire immunity to a particular pathogen?

choices.text: Vaccination and recovery from a previous infection
Wearing gloves and cleaning contaminated equipment
Taking antibiotics and avoiding patient contact
Vaccination and having no symptoms during one exposure

questions.explanation: Vaccination and prior infection can produce pathogen-specific immune protection; neither guarantees lifelong complete protection.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: These reduce exposure but do not create pathogen-specific immunity.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Treatment or avoidance is not the same as acquired immune protection.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: An asymptomatic exposure alone does not establish immunity.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Vaccination and prior infection can produce pathogen-specific immune protection; neither guarantees lifelong complete protection.

questions.question: A used needle punctures an EMT’s skin. Another qualified provider can take over patient care. What is the best immediate plan?

choices.text: Transfer care safely, wash the site, report the exposure, and seek prompt medical evaluation
Wash the site and wait for symptoms before notifying the exposure officer
Obtain the source patient’s test results before seeking evaluation
Complete the transport and incident report before addressing the puncture

questions.explanation: Exposure management needs prompt first aid, reporting, and clinical evaluation; documentation supports the process without delaying care.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Symptoms may not appear promptly, and reporting should not wait.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Source testing can inform evaluation but should not delay it.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Immediate wound care and evaluation take priority over completing routine tasks.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Exposure management needs prompt first aid, reporting, and clinical evaluation; documentation supports the process without delaying care.
questions.whyTempting: Washing is an appropriate initial step.
questions.whyNotBest: Symptoms may not appear promptly, and reporting should not wait.
questions.keyDistinction: Exposure management needs prompt first aid, reporting, and clinical evaluation; documentation supports the process without delaying care.

questions.question: A leaking tanker has an unreadable placard. Patients are near the spill. The EMT crew lacks hazardous-material entry training and equipment. What should the crew do first?

choices.text: Stage safely away from the spill and request trained hazardous-material resources
Approach far enough to read the placard, then select a staging location
Use examination gloves and an N95 to reach the nearest patient before the hazmat team
Park near the patient cluster and prepare treatment while the spill is identified

questions.explanation: Protect responders first, identify hazards from a safe distance, and use trained resources for entry and decontamination.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Approaching an unidentified release to read the placard may expose the crew.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Routine medical PPE does not establish protection from an unidentified chemical release.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Staging near the spill exposes personnel and equipment before the hazard is controlled.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Protect responders first, identify hazards from a safe distance, and use trained resources for entry and decontamination.
questions.whyTempting: Knowing the material helps responders plan.
questions.whyNotBest: Approaching an unidentified release to read the placard may expose the crew.
questions.keyDistinction: Protect responders first, identify hazards from a safe distance, and use trained resources for entry and decontamination.

questions.question: Which inner-to-outer clothing arrangement best manages moisture, insulation, and weather protection?

choices.text: Moisture-wicking layer → insulating layer → weather-resistant layer
Weather-resistant layer → moisture-wicking layer → insulating layer
Insulating layer → weather-resistant layer → moisture-wicking layer
Moisture-wicking layer → weather-resistant layer → insulating layer

questions.explanation: The inner layer moves moisture away, the middle insulates, and the outer layer resists wind and precipitation.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: A weather barrier next to the skin does not fulfill the inner wicking role.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: This puts the wicking layer outside and the weather barrier in the middle.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: This leaves insulation outside the weather barrier.

questions.question: After a death, one family member is silent and another alternates between disbelief and anger without threatening anyone. How should the EMT respond?

choices.text: Offer honest, calm support and allow each person to express grief differently
Explain that anger must end before they can move to the next stage
Interpret the silent relative’s behavior as definite acceptance
Give a detailed account immediately so both relatives will process the loss in the same way

questions.explanation: Grief reactions can differ and overlap; supportive care does not require a fixed sequence or a single style of grieving.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: The stages are not a mandatory sequence the EMT must enforce.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Silence alone does not establish a specific grief stage.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Overloading people with detail does not ensure understanding or identical reactions.

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Grief reactions can differ and overlap; supportive care does not require a fixed sequence or a single style of grieving.
questions.whyTempting: The familiar stage names can suggest an ordered sequence.
questions.whyNotBest: The stages are not a mandatory sequence the EMT must enforce.
questions.keyDistinction: Grief reactions can differ and overlap; supportive care does not require a fixed sequence or a single style of grieving.

questions.question: Which pattern best fits the immediate alarm response to stress?

choices.text: Faster pulse and breathing, dilated pupils, and reduced gastrointestinal blood flow
Slower pulse and breathing, dilated pupils, and increased gastrointestinal blood flow
Faster pulse and breathing, constricted pupils, and increased gastrointestinal blood flow
Slower pulse and breathing, constricted pupils, and reduced gastrointestinal blood flow

questions.explanation: The alarm response increases readiness for action while shifting resources away from digestion.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: Slower cardiopulmonary activity and increased digestive flow do not match the described alarm response.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Pupil constriction and increased digestive flow conflict with the expected response.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Reduced digestive flow is compatible, but the other changes are not the typical alarm pattern.

sourceReferences.locator: VIII.C–D: General adaptation and physiologic stress

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified

questions.question: Following a traumatic call, an EMT has recurring nightmares, intrusive recollections, and strong reactions to reminders that interfere with work. What is the best approach?

choices.text: Arrange qualified mental-health assessment and appropriate support
Use an operational critique as the sole way to resolve the symptoms
Use a group support session as the only response, even if symptoms persist
Assume the symptoms are ordinary fatigue and address only the shift schedule

questions.explanation: Reexperiencing the event and strong reactions to reminders are features of traumatic stress. Trained critical-incident support and private professional counseling are resources for the provider.

incorrectChoiceExplanations.B: A performance review is different from mental-health assessment and support.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.C: Critical-incident support does not replace the option of private professional counseling for ongoing difficulty.
incorrectChoiceExplanations.D: Rest matters, but fatigue alone does not account for the trauma-linked pattern.

sourceReferences.locator: VIII.G: PTSD and critical incident support

questions.verificationStatus: Reviewed against uploaded course materials; not independently verified
questions.diagnosticIntent: Reexperiencing the event and strong reactions to reminders are features of traumatic stress. Trained critical-incident support and private professional counseling are resources for the provider.
questions.whyTempting: An operational review may identify lessons from the call.
questions.whyNotBest: A performance review is different from mental-health assessment and support.
questions.keyDistinction: Reexperiencing the event and strong reactions to reminders are features of traumatic stress. Trained critical-incident support and private professional counseling are resources for the provider.
